activities.caption: drag the divider — transplants, then culture
activities.name: compTransplantCompare

config.prompt: The transplant debate — drag the divider:

before.label: Watson — transplants migrate cheaply
before.text: The Code civil exported across Europe and Latin America; Japan received a BGB-based code in 1898 and it functions.

after.label: Legrand — law is culture
after.text: The words changed without the practice: Japan's litigation rates run a fraction of America's, and England sues less than either.

config.why: The evidence lands between: reception created a working system whose social meaning stays distinct — study the problem (dispute frequency, remedy uptake), not the rule's text.

morality entering through judicial sympathy, jury verdicts and statute

config.why: Constitutional courts worldwide now mediate the placement — abortion and same-sex marriage the current frontier cases everywhere.

activities.anchor: the gradient is continuous, not binary
activities.caption: audit the three systems
activities.name: compRuleLawBranch

config.root: You are the comparative auditor. One question per system: does law bind the state itself?

start.text: System one: courts review state action under published, prospective rules. Verdict?

choices.label: Rule of law
choices.feedback: The German Rechtsstaat, the French état de droit, Dicey's idea: state action needs legal authority.

choices.label: Rule by law
choices.feedback: Hold that verdict for the next case.

rol.text: System two: every formal criterion met — published, clear, prospective rules — yet courts are subordinated to party leadership and the content serves power. Verdict?

choices.label: Rule by law
choices.feedback: Raz's warning embodied: formal criteria can be satisfied while the law serves power.

choices.label: Rule of law
choices.feedback: Review the criterion that matters: who does the law bind?

rbl.text: System three: judiciaries formally independent but episodically captured — court restructuring contested with the EU. Verdict?

choices.label: Somewhere on the continuum between the two
choices.feedback: The intermediate case — Poland's 2015–2023 restructuring is the standing illustration.

mid.text: The audit's finding: the test is whether law binds the state itself — and the answer comes in degrees.

config.why: The comparison clarifies the contested cases too: the in-between is not a failure of the test but a measurement on it.

activities.anchor: the "law" is a sediment, not a monument
activities.caption: find the line the two-families myth wrote
activities.name: compDraftSpot

config.prompt: One line of this drafting-cultures summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Civil-law codes state the whole private order in general principles, filled downward by interpretation.
Common-law systems accumulate — statutes patch, courts systematise.
Continental codes generalise and trust courts with abstraction; English statutes particularise and trust no one.
Louisiana cannot have a civil code — mixed systems are constitutionally barred.
Quebec's Code civil lives in a federal common-law country; South Africa runs Roman-Dutch common law under parliamentary statute.
config.correction: Mixed jurisdictions show both at once — Louisiana's civil code under a common-law shell, Quebec, South Africa; nothing bars them.
config.why: The drafting cultures persist even as volume differences shrink — English legislation now dominates volume.

events.title: The French Code civil
events.text: Five books drafted for a post-revolutionary society — the template exported wherever French power or admiration reached.

events.title: The BGB in force
events.text: The pandectist scholarship behind it took two decades and a scholarly generation.

events.title: The German Enabling Act
events.text: Delegation without limits, renewed by plebiscite — the discipline's standing caution.

events.title: England's Law Commission
events.text: Standing commissions propose and draft; Parliament enacts — incremental, consultative, politically exposed.

events.title: France recodifies contract
events.text: The recent recodification, by ordinance — codification still the reform instrument of history.

config.q: The Code civil's Article 5 forbids judges from issuing general regulatory judgments — yet the Cour de cassation's consistent case law is law in every functional sense. What happened to the article?
choices: Honoured in form, evaded in practice — predictability won
It never applied to private law
config.why: Methods converge in outcome more than in theory — everyone asks what the provision meant to do, eventually.
